page: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v7 is an x86_64 cloud server running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, driven by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at frequencies up to 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 64 physical cores, accompanied by 256 GB of system RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU density. Compute subsystems include 480 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction-level acceleration via AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8. High-speed local persistence is supplied via a bundled 7559 GB NVMe SSD array. The instance contains no discrete graphics hardware and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance profiles across synthetic and practical workloads place this machine in the top tier for multi-threaded CPU and high-throughput data tasks. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 145373.21 and a PassMark CPU score of 128741.43, bolstered by extended instruction operations reaching 171745.5. In data transfer testing, memory bandwidth registered 657.87 GB/sec on large uncached blocks and 10709.34 GB/sec on cached reads. High-volume operational performance is further evidenced by top-tier results in Redis SET testing at 196.23 million operations per second, static web serving throughput of 145.81 GB/sec, and a Clang software compilation score of 70716.0.

Cost efficiency is focused on compute density and direct disk access. By coupling 128 processor threads directly with 7.5 TB of fast NVMe storage, the instance avoids the financial overhead of high memory capacity while delivering maximum thread concurrency. A potential tradeoff is the lower memory-to-vCPU allocation, making it unsuitable for applications requiring large per-thread memory footprints or GPU acceleration. Workloads matching this resource configuration include large CI/CD software compilation farms, web servers, CPU-driven inference pipelines, distributed database nodes, and multi-threaded data compression tasks.

A bundled 7559 GB local NVMe SSD provides extensive fast storage, while no discrete GPUs are present. Benchmark results show exceptional multi-core throughput, reflected in top-tier results across stress-ng multi-core processing, static web serving at 145.81 GB/sec, and 196.23 million Redis SET operations per second. The 2 GB per core memory profile ensures resource-efficient execution for compute-intensive pipelines that rely on fast scratch disks rather than massive RAM allocations. The instance fits high-volume web serving, distributed databases, large-scale software builds, and batch compression tasks.
